common_name: Only the Lonely Nicotiana (Giant Fragrant Woodland Tobacco)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; site where its evening perfume reaches a patio, porch, or open window.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost. This dramatic architectural annual forms a basal rosette of huge paddle-shaped leaves before sending up tall, sturdy spikes topped with clusters of long, pendant, trumpet-shaped white flowers. The blooms release an intense jasmine-like fragrance that carries widely at night, making it one of the most powerfully scented garden annuals available from seed. Its height and bold foliage make it an effective specimen or back-of-border plant, and it self-sows in milder climates once established.

common_name: Saratoga Purple Bicolor Nicotiana (Compact Day-Blooming Bedding Tobacco)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; needs no staking or deadheading.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost. The Saratoga series was bred for compact, uniform bedding plants whose flowers stay open through the day rather than closing in sunlight, a common complaint with older fragrant nicotiana strains. Purple Bicolor bears abundant star-shaped flowers in rich purple with a crisp white throat, held on tidy, well-branched plants that need no staking or deadheading. It performs reliably in beds and mixed containers through summer heat and continues flowering steadily until frost.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; self-sows readily where happy.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost. This species nicotiana has a wiry, airy, well-branched habit distinct from stockier bedding cultivars, carrying masses of small, nodding, bell-shaped chartreuse-green flowers whose mouths reveal a striking ring of sky-blue pollen-bearing anthers. It is a favorite of garden designers for softening bold color combinations and mixing into cut arrangements, where its unusual lime tone reads almost as a foliage accent. It self-sows readily where happy and draws pollinators steadily through the season.

common_name: Marine Bells Browallia (Deep Blue Bush Violet)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; pinch young seedlings once to encourage a fuller, more floriferous shape.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; pinch young seedlings once to encourage a fuller, more floriferous shape. Marine Bells is a compact, mounded hybrid bush violet bred for abundant, upward-facing, deep gentian-blue bell-shaped flowers marked with a small white eye. It is one of the truest blue-flowered shade annuals available from seed, making it valuable for hanging baskets, window boxes, and shaded beds where blue tones are scarce. Plants bloom continuously without deadheading.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost; tolerates summer humidity better than many other blue-flowered shade annuals.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost. Sapphire is a notably more compact and free-flowering selection than older browallia strains, staying under a foot tall while producing a near-continuous cover of deep violet-blue flowers with a small white throat. Its small scale suits shaded window boxes, small pots, and edging where taller browallia cultivars would sprawl. It tolerates summer humidity better than many other blue-flowered shade annuals and needs no deadheading to maintain bloom.
